summary: Everton manager Sean Dyche says he is confident the club's season will not be derailed by a 10-point penalty for breaching Premier League financial rules, but he has warned his players not to rely on the appeal to escape the relegation battle. He addressed the squad at Finch Farm, said the players had responded defiantly, and expects fans to rally against Manchester United on Sunday. Dyche called the punishment disproportionate and unjust.
one_line: Sean Dyche says Everton will use the 10-point deduction as fuel, urging players to treat it as reality rather than wait for the appeal.
key_facts: Everton received a 10-point penalty, the biggest sporting sanction in Premier League history, for a £19.5m overspend in 2021-22.
The penalty was imposed by an independent commission for breaching Premier League financial rules.
Sean Dyche was ill on holiday in Dubai when Everton's director of football, Kevin Thelwell, told him of the punishment.
Dyche addressed the first-team squad at Finch Farm on Friday morning after all players had returned from international duty.
Before the deduction Everton had won six of nine games in all competitions and risen to 14th; the penalty dropped them back to 19th.
Everton are joint-bottom of the Premier League on four points after the deduction.
Everton's appeal will be heard by a different three-person panel before the end of the season.
Dyche told players there are 'no guarantees' the appeal will change things and they must 'commit to this reality' of having lost 10 points.
The players shared defiant messages on their WhatsApp group when the news broke, including 'Right lads, just another challenge'.
Everton fans have planned a series of protests against the Premier League for Sunday's home game against Manchester United, when a win could lift Everton out of the bottom three.
Dyche believes the punishment has created a collective siege mentality at Goodison Park after years of division between fans and the club's hierarchy.
Dyche declined to comment on implications for Manchester City, charged with 115 financial breaches which they deny, and Chelsea, also under investigation.
